theory.intro: When a particle's velocity changes with time, questions ask for times, speeds, positions or unknown constants. The particle is momentarily **at rest** only when both components of $\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$ are zero at the same time; it moves parallel to an axis when just one component is zero.
facts: A particle is at rest when $\dot{x}=0$ and $\dot{y}=0$ at the same value of $t$.
If only $\dot{y}=0$, the particle is moving parallel to the $x$-axis, not at rest.
Speed is $|\underset{\sim}{v}|=\sqrt{\dot{x}^{2}+\dot{y}^{2}}$, so it is never negative. Adding the velocity components is not the general formula for speed.
Since the square root is increasing, minimise or maximise $\dot{x}^{2}+\dot{y}^{2}$ over the allowed time domain instead of the speed itself, checking applicable endpoints.

For rest questions, solve $\dot{x}=0$ and $\dot{y}=0$ separately, then keep only the times common to both. For motion parallel to the $x$-axis, require $\dot{y}=0$ and $\dot{x}\ne 0$; for motion parallel to the $y$-axis, require $\dot{x}=0$ and $\dot{y}\ne 0$.
Reject any solution with $t<0$, or outside the interval the question states.
Substitute the time back into $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)$ to find where the event happens.
steps: Find $\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$: differentiate supplied $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)$, or integrate each component of supplied acceleration and use the initial velocity to find the integration constants. For constant acceleration and initial velocity $\underset{\sim}{u}$ at $t=0$, use $\underset{\sim}{v}(t)=\underset{\sim}{u}+t\underset{\sim}{a}$
For rest or parallel motion, write the condition as equations in $\dot{x}$ and $\dot{y}$. For speed, form $|\underset{\sim}{v}(t)|^{2}=\dot{x}^{2}+\dot{y}^{2}$

Solve the condition for the required time or constants, using any supplied event time and rejecting times outside the allowed interval. For extreme speed, minimise or maximise speed squared over the allowed interval, checking applicable endpoints
Substitute the required time into $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)$ for position, or take the square root of speed squared for speed, to answer the question asked

workedExamples.question_text: A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(t^3-9t^2+24t)\underset{\sim}{i}+(t^2-8t+7)\underset{\sim}{j}$ metres, where $t\ge0$ is in seconds. Find when it is momentarily at rest, its position vector then, and its exact distance from the origin.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Differentiate each component.
$\begin{align*}\underset{\sim}{v}(t)&=(3t^2-18t+24)\underset{\sim}{i}+(2t-8)\underset{\sim}{j}\end{align*}$
At rest, both velocity components must vanish together.
$\begin{align*}3(t-2)(t-4)&=0\\t&=2\text{ or }4\\2t-8&=0\\t&=4\end{align*}$
The only common time is $t=4$ seconds.
$\begin{align*}\underset{\sim}{r}(4)&=(64-144+96)\underset{\sim}{i}+(16-32+7)\underset{\sim}{j}\\&=16\underset{\sim}{i}-9\underset{\sim}{j}\end{align*}$
The position vector is $(16\underset{\sim}{i}-9\underset{\sim}{j})$ metres. Its distance from the origin is
$\begin{align*}|\underset{\sim}{r}(4)|&=\sqrt{16^2+(-9)^2}\\&=\sqrt{337}\text{ m}.\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text: A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(t^2-8t)\underset{\sim}{i}+(t^3-75t)\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge0$. Determine whether it is ever at rest, and find when it moves parallel to each coordinate axis.
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=3\sin 2t\,\underset{\sim}{i}+4t\,\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $0\le t\le\pi$. Find all times when it moves parallel to the $y$-axis.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{align*}\underset{\sim}{v}(t)&=6\cos 2t\,\underset{\sim}{i}+4\underset{\sim}{j}\end{align*}$
Parallel motion to the $y$-axis requires $\dot{x}=0$ and $\dot{y}\ne0$. Here $\dot{y}=4\ne0$ throughout.
$\begin{align*}6\cos 2t&=0\\\cos 2t&=0\end{align*}$
Since $0\le2t\le2\pi$, the solutions are
$\begin{align*}2t&=\frac{\pi}{2}\text{ or }\frac{3\pi}{2}\\t&=\frac{\pi}{4}\text{ or }\frac{3\pi}{4}.\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text: A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(e^t-2t)\underset{\sim}{i}+(t^2-4t)\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge0$. Find the exact time when it moves parallel to the $y$-axis.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{align*}\underset{\sim}{v}(t)&=(e^t-2)\underset{\sim}{i}+(2t-4)\underset{\sim}{j}\end{align*}$
Set the horizontal velocity component to zero.
$\begin{align*}e^t-2&=0\\e^t&=2\\t&=\ln2\end{align*}$
Check the other component.
$\begin{align*}\dot{y}(\ln2)&=2\ln2-4\\&\ne0\end{align*}$
Since $0<\ln2<1$, this component is negative. The particle moves parallel to the $y$-axis at $t=\ln2$.

workedExamples.question_text: A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=\bigl(t-6\ln(t+1)\bigr)\underset{\sim}{i}+3t\,\underset{\sim}{j}$ metres, where $t\ge0$ is in seconds. Find its minimum speed and when it occurs.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{align*}\underset{\sim}{v}(t)&=\left(1-\frac{6}{t+1}\right)\underset{\sim}{i}+3\underset{\sim}{j}\\|\underset{\sim}{v}(t)|^2&=\left(1-\frac{6}{t+1}\right)^2+9\end{align*}$
The squared term is non-negative, so speed squared is at least $9$. This bound is attained when
$\begin{align*}1-\frac{6}{t+1}&=0\\t+1&=6\\t&=5.\end{align*}$
This time is in the domain. The minimum speed is $\sqrt9=3\text{ m s}^{-1}$, at $t=5$ seconds.

workedExamples.question_text: A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(t^2-4t)\underset{\sim}{i}+(t^2-8t)\underset{\sim}{j}$ metres, where $t$ is in seconds. Find its exact minimum speed on (a) $0\le t\le5$ and (b) $4\le t\le5$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{align*}\underset{\sim}{v}(t)&=(2t-4)\underset{\sim}{i}+(2t-8)\underset{\sim}{j}\\|\underset{\sim}{v}(t)|^2&=(2t-4)^2+(2t-8)^2\\&=8t^2-48t+80\\&=8(t-3)^2+8\end{align*}$
(a) The vertex $t=3$ lies in $[0,5]$. Speed squared has its global minimum there, so the minimum speed is $\sqrt8=2\sqrt2\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
(b) On $[4,5]$, $(t-3)^2$ increases as $t$ increases. The minimum therefore occurs at the left endpoint, $t=4$.
$\begin{align*}|\underset{\sim}{v}(4)|^2&=8(4-3)^2+8\\&=16\\|\underset{\sim}{v}(4)|&=4\text{ m s}^{-1}.\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text: A drone has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=3t\,\underset{\sim}{i}+(t^2-4t)\underset{\sim}{j}$ kilometres, where $t$ is in hours and $0\le t\le5$. Find its exact maximum speed.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{align*}\underset{\sim}{v}(t)&=3\underset{\sim}{i}+(2t-4)\underset{\sim}{j}\\|\underset{\sim}{v}(t)|^2&=9+(2t-4)^2\end{align*}$
The squared term decreases to zero at $t=2$, then increases. Its maximum on this interval is at an endpoint.
$\begin{align*}|\underset{\sim}{v}(0)|^2&=9+(-4)^2=25\\|\underset{\sim}{v}(5)|^2&=9+6^2=45\end{align*}$
The maximum speed is $\sqrt{45}=3\sqrt5\text{ km h}^{-1}$, at $t=5$ hours.

workedExamples.question_text: A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(t^2+at)\underset{\sim}{i}+(t^3+bt)\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge0$, where $a$ and $b$ are constants. It is momentarily at rest at $t=3$. Find $a$ and $b$.

A particle initially has velocity $(2\underset{\sim}{i}+\underset{\sim}{j})\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and constant acceleration $(-\underset{\sim}{i}+2\underset{\sim}{j})\text{ m s}^{-2}$. Find its speed after $3$ seconds.
workedExamples.solution_text:
For constant acceleration, use $\underset{\sim}{v}(t)=\underset{\sim}{u}+t\underset{\sim}{a}$.
$\begin{align*}\underset{\sim}{v}(3)&=(2\underset{\sim}{i}+\underset{\sim}{j})+3(-\underset{\sim}{i}+2\underset{\sim}{j})\\&=-\underset{\sim}{i}+7\underset{\sim}{j}\end{align*}$
Speed is the magnitude of velocity.
$\begin{align*}|\underset{\sim}{v}(3)|&=\sqrt{(-1)^2+7^2}\\&=5\sqrt2\text{ m s}^{-1}.\end{align*}$

foundation.question_text:
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(t^{2}-6t+5)\underset{\sim}{i}+(t^{2}-6t+8)\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge 0$.
Find the time at which the particle is momentarily at rest.
foundation.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$
$=(2t-6)\underset{\sim}{i}+(2t-6)\underset{\sim}{j}$
$2t-6=0$
$t=3$
Both components vanish at $t=3$, so the particle is at rest at $t=3$.

foundation.question_text:
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(t^{3}-12t)\underset{\sim}{i}+(t^{2}-4t)\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge 0$.
Find the time at which the particle is momentarily at rest.
foundation.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$
$=(3t^{2}-12)\underset{\sim}{i}+(2t-4)\underset{\sim}{j}$
$3t^{2}-12=0$
$t^{2}=4$
$t=2$ (rejecting $t=-2$ since $t\ge 0$)
$2t-4=0$
$t=2$
Both components vanish at $t=2$, so the particle is at rest at $t=2$.

foundation.question_text:
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(2t^{2}-10t)\underset{\sim}{i}+(t^{3}-3t^{2})\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge 0$.
Find the time at which the particle is moving parallel to the $y$-axis.
foundation.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$
$=(4t-10)\underset{\sim}{i}+(3t^{2}-6t)\underset{\sim}{j}$
Moving parallel to the $y$-axis means $\dot{x}=0$ and $\dot{y}\ne 0$.
$4t-10=0$
$t=2.5$
$\dot{y}(2.5)$
$=3(2.5)^{2}-6(2.5)$
$=18.75-15$
$=3.75$
Since $\dot{y}\ne 0$, the particle is moving parallel to the $y$-axis at $t=2.5$.

foundation.question_text:
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(4t+1)\underset{\sim}{i}+(t^{2}-6t)\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge 0$.
Find the time at which the particle is moving parallel to the $x$-axis.
foundation.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$
$=4\underset{\sim}{i}+(2t-6)\underset{\sim}{j}$
Moving parallel to the $x$-axis means $\dot{y}=0$ and $\dot{x}\ne 0$.
$2t-6=0$
$t=3$
$\dot{x}=4$, which is never zero, so the particle is moving parallel to the $x$-axis at $t=3$.

foundation.question_text:
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(t^{2}-6t)\underset{\sim}{i}+4t\,\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge 0$.
Find its minimum speed.
foundation.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$
$=(2t-6)\underset{\sim}{i}+4\underset{\sim}{j}$
$|\underset{\sim}{v}|^{2}$
$=(2t-6)^{2}+16$
The square root is increasing, so the speed is least when $(2t-6)^{2}$ is least.
$(2t-6)^{2}=0$
$t=3$
$|\underset{\sim}{v}(3)|$
$=\sqrt{0+16}$
$=4$

foundation.question_text:
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(t^{3}-3t^{2})\underset{\sim}{i}+(2t^{3}-6t^{2})\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t>0$.
Find its position vector at the instant it is momentarily at rest.

development.question_text:
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(2t^{3}-9t^{2}+12t)\underset{\sim}{i}+(t^{2}-4t+4)\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge 0$.
Show that the particle is momentarily at rest exactly once, and find that time.
development.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$
$=(6t^{2}-18t+12)\underset{\sim}{i}+(2t-4)\underset{\sim}{j}$
$6t^{2}-18t+12=0$
$6(t-1)(t-2)=0$
$t=1$ or $t=2$
$2t-4=0$
$t=2$
Only $t=2$ makes both components zero, so the particle is at rest exactly once, at $t=2$.

development.question_text:
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=\sin 2t\,\underset{\sim}{i}+2t\,\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $0\le t\le \pi$.
Find all times at which the particle is moving parallel to the $y$-axis.
development.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$
$=2\cos 2t\,\underset{\sim}{i}+2\underset{\sim}{j}$
$\dot{y}=2$, which is never zero.
$2\cos 2t=0$
For $0\le t\le \pi$, $2t$ runs from $0$ to $2\pi$.
$2t=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ or $2t=\dfrac{3\pi}{2}$
$t=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ or $t=\dfrac{3\pi}{4}$

development.question_text:
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=t^{2}\underset{\sim}{i}+(t^{2}-6t)\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $0\le t\le 4$.
Find its minimum speed, in exact form.
development.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$
$=2t\,\underset{\sim}{i}+(2t-6)\underset{\sim}{j}$
$|\underset{\sim}{v}|^{2}$
$=4t^{2}+(2t-6)^{2}$
$=4t^{2}+4t^{2}-24t+36$
$=8t^{2}-24t+36$
This is least at the vertex.
$t=\dfrac{24}{16}$
$t=1.5$, which lies in $0\le t\le 4$.
$|\underset{\sim}{v}(1.5)|^{2}$
$=8(2.25)-36+36$
$=18$
$|\underset{\sim}{v}(1.5)|$
$=\sqrt{18}$
$=3\sqrt{2}$

development.question_text:
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(t^{3}-6t^{2}+9t)\underset{\sim}{i}+(t^{2}-6t+5)\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge 0$.
Find its position vector at the instant it is momentarily at rest.
development.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$
$=(3t^{2}-12t+9)\underset{\sim}{i}+(2t-6)\underset{\sim}{j}$
$3(t-1)(t-3)=0$
$t=1$ or $t=3$
$2t-6=0$
$t=3$
Both components vanish only at $t=3$.
$\underset{\sim}{r}(3)$
$=(27-54+27)\underset{\sim}{i}+(9-18+5)\underset{\sim}{j}$
$=0\underset{\sim}{i}-4\underset{\sim}{j}$
$=-4\underset{\sim}{j}$

development.question_text:
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(t^{2}-4t)\underset{\sim}{i}+(t^{3}-27t)\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge 0$.
Is the particle ever momentarily at rest?
Justify your answer.
development.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$
$=(2t-4)\underset{\sim}{i}+(3t^{2}-27)\underset{\sim}{j}$
$2t-4=0$
$t=2$
$3t^{2}-27=0$
$t^{2}=9$
$t=3$ (rejecting $t=-3$ since $t\ge 0$)
The two components are never zero at the same time.
The particle is never at rest: at $t=2$ it is moving parallel to the $y$-axis, and at $t=3$ it is moving parallel to the $x$-axis.

development.question_text:
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(e^{t}-3t)\underset{\sim}{i}+(t^{2}-2t)\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge 0$.
Find the exact time at which the particle is moving parallel to the $y$-axis.
development.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$
$=(e^{t}-3)\underset{\sim}{i}+(2t-2)\underset{\sim}{j}$
$e^{t}-3=0$
$e^{t}=3$
$t=\ln 3$
$\dot{y}(\ln 3)$
$=2\ln 3-2$
Since $\ln 3>1$, $\dot{y}\ne 0$, so the particle is moving parallel to the $y$-axis at $t=\ln 3$.

development.question_text:
A drone's position, in kilometres from its base, is $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=4t\,\underset{\sim}{i}+(t^{2}-2t)\underset{\sim}{j}$, where $t$ is in hours and $0\le t\le 4$.
Find its exact maximum speed over this interval.
development.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$
$=4\underset{\sim}{i}+(2t-2)\underset{\sim}{j}$
$|\underset{\sim}{v}|^{2}$
$=16+(2t-2)^{2}$
This is greatest when $(2t-2)^{2}$ is greatest, so test the ends of $0\le t\le 4$.
$(2(0)-2)^{2}=4$
$(2(4)-2)^{2}=36$
The maximum is at $t=4$.
$|\underset{\sim}{v}(4)|$
$=\sqrt{16+36}$
$=\sqrt{52}$
$=2\sqrt{13}$ km/h

mastery.question_text:
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(2t^{3}-15t^{2}+24t)\underset{\sim}{i}+(t^{2}-8t+12)\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge 0$.
Find its exact distance from the origin at the instant it is momentarily at rest.
mastery.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$
$=(6t^{2}-30t+24)\underset{\sim}{i}+(2t-8)\underset{\sim}{j}$
$6(t-1)(t-4)=0$
$t=1$ or $t=4$
$2t-8=0$
$t=4$
Both components vanish only at $t=4$.
$\underset{\sim}{r}(4)$
$=(128-240+96)\underset{\sim}{i}+(16-32+12)\underset{\sim}{j}$
$=-16\underset{\sim}{i}-4\underset{\sim}{j}$
$|\underset{\sim}{r}(4)|$
$=\sqrt{256+16}$
$=\sqrt{272}$
$=4\sqrt{17}$

mastery.question_text:
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=\left(t-4\ln(t+1)\right)\underset{\sim}{i}+5t\,\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge 0$.
Find its minimum speed and the time at which it occurs.
mastery.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$
$=\left(1-\dfrac{4}{t+1}\right)\underset{\sim}{i}+5\underset{\sim}{j}$
$|\underset{\sim}{v}|^{2}$
$=\left(1-\dfrac{4}{t+1}\right)^{2}+25$
The speed is least when the squared bracket is zero.
$1-\dfrac{4}{t+1}=0$
$t+1=4$
$t=3$
$|\underset{\sim}{v}(3)|$
$=\sqrt{0+25}$
$=5$
The minimum speed is $5$, at $t=3$.

mastery.question_text:
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(t^{2}+at)\underset{\sim}{i}+(t^{3}+bt)\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge 0$, where $a$ and $b$ are constants.
The particle is momentarily at rest when $t=2$.
Find $a$ and $b$.
mastery.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$
$=(2t+a)\underset{\sim}{i}+(3t^{2}+b)\underset{\sim}{j}$
At rest at $t=2$ means both components are zero there.
$4+a=0$
$a=-4$
$12+b=0$
$b=-12$
